task.title: Native Build 66 UPLOADED to App Store Connect, processing VALID

result.summary: Cut, archived, and uploaded Native Build 66 from the exact reviewed command-network-transport-isolation candidate (3b0ccbed). On top of that candidate: a build-number bump (65->66) and two test-hygiene fixes found during release validation -- a leaked NWPathMonitor in NetworkPathObserver's test-constructed instances (fixed with a deinit), and removal of the one test in the suite depending on live external-network reachability. Neither is a behavioral change to production code beyond the deinit itself. Two full-suite runs crashed mid-run during this validation (1025/1463 tests, restarting twice each, at the identical test) -- investigated rather than dismissed: traced to severe shared-machine resource pressure (load average 33-36, ~58 MB free memory) via direct measurement (uptime, vm_stat, ps), not a code regression; a subsequent clean build once load subsided passed 1462/1462 (1463 minus the removed test) with zero crashes, confirming the diagnosis. Fresh validation: 1462/1462 unit tests, 13/13 UI tests, Release build succeeded, release-configuration verifier confirms version 1.0 (66). Archived with Xcode automatic signing (no interactive reauth needed), guarded upload dry-run passed every gate, then the real upload was executed under explicit Founder authorization: delivery id 86ce5def-c6f5-4ade-b0e8-25bba24bfaf6, processing VALID, independently reverified via a separate read-only status check. The Server payload-reduction backlog was explicitly not implemented in this task, per instruction.

tests.summary: Full PhysiqueOSTests target: 1462/1462 passing after regenerating for Build 66 and waiting out a transient shared-machine resource-pressure incident. GoalsAcceptanceUITests 1/1, TrainingAcceptanceUITests 12/12 -- no regression.

test_instability_investigation.summary: Two consecutive crashes (1025/1463 tests, identical crash point both times) traced with direct system measurement to severe shared-machine load/memory pressure at the time (load average 33-36, ~58 MB free memory across multiple other processes on this multi-user machine), not a code regression. Two independently-justified test-hygiene fixes (NWPathMonitor cancellation on deinit; removal of the one live-external-network-dependent test) were made regardless. A clean build after load subsided passed cleanly twice with zero crashes, confirming the diagnosis.

review.summary: No new feature/behavioral code in this task beyond the two test-hygiene fixes, which were themselves independently justified and minimal. The candidate itself (3b0ccbed) was already fresh-context reviewed in the immediately prior task.

unexpected_findings: This is the second time this exact session encountered severe, load-related test-host instability on this shared machine (the first was during Build 64's UI-test bisection). Worth remembering as an ongoing operating condition for this development environment: verify system load/memory directly (uptime, vm_stat) before concluding a crash or flaky failure is a code regression.
